directAnswer: Pope Benedict VI reigned from January 973 to June 974. A Roman elected with Otto I's approval, he lost his protection when Otto died and was imprisoned and killed by a Roman faction that installed the antipope Boniface VII.

paras: Benedict was a Roman, the son of a man named Hildebrand, and served as a cardinal-deacon before his election. He was chosen after the death of John XIII, but his consecration on 19 January 973 had to wait until Otto I gave his approval, which shows how much the emperor's consent counted after 962.

sections.h2: The Death of Otto I and a Roman Revolt
paras: Otto I died in May 973, and his son Otto II was occupied with affairs in Germany. Roman nobles hostile to imperial influence, led by Crescentius, a member of the family that would dominate Rome for decades, seized the opportunity. In June 974 they imprisoned Benedict in the Castel Sant'Angelo and raised the deacon Franco to the papal throne as Boniface VII, now listed as an antipope.

When an imperial envoy arrived to demand Benedict's release, his captors had him strangled in prison. The Liber Pontificalis names a priest called Stephen as the killer, acting on Franco's orders. Little else about Benedict's personal outlook or reign is recorded; his death is the most documented fact of his life.

keyFacts: Roman by birth; son of Hildebrand
Consecrated only after Otto I approved his election
Imprisoned in the Castel Sant'Angelo by Crescentius's faction
Killed in prison; antipope Boniface VII was installed

faqs.question: Who killed Pope Benedict VI?
faqs.answer: According to the Liber Pontificalis, a priest named Stephen strangled him in prison on the orders of Franco, who had been set up as the antipope Boniface VII.

faqs.question: Why was Benedict VI vulnerable after 973?
faqs.answer: His protector, Otto I, died in 973, and the new emperor was far away, leaving Roman nobles free to move against the pope.
